channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ford will not endorse any Toronto mayoral candidate: premier’s office
‘Fabulous:’ Doug Ford welcomes airport investment plan, says Billy Bishop should be next
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford is voicing his support for a proposal to seek private investors for four Canadian airports, noting that it “should have been done years ago.”

item.title: ‘It’s the law:’ Ontario threatens to cut funding to municipalities that fail to follow ‘Buy Canadian’ policy
item.description: Ontario municipalities could face cuts to provincial funding if they fail to comply with “Buy Ontario” procurement requirements, warned Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing Rob Flack Wednesday.

item.title: SeatGeek gets maximum $25,000 penalty for allegedly breaking Ontario ticket resale law
item.description: One of the biggest ticket resale companies in the word is facing a $25,000 fine after it allegedly failed to abide by a new Ontario law that prohibits gouging customers.

item.title: Four years into $10/day program, child-care waitlists growing in some Ontario cities
item.description: While about half of the provinces are offering average fees of $10 a day, Ontario has not yet met that goal, with fees capped at $22 a day – still significantly lower from upwards of $70 for some spots before Ontario joined the program four years ago. But some parents and at least one prominent child-care advocate are urging Ontario to worry less at the moment about further lowering fees to $10, and instead prioritize expansion.

item.title: Ontario minister pledges better communication during wildfire season
item.description: Ontario’s Natural Resources Minister Mike Harris pledged Monday better communication on wildfires after many First Nations communities said they received little to no warning about approaching flames this summer.

item.title: Ontario Science Centre laying off entire science department
item.description: The Ontario Science Centre has laid off 30 workers including the entire science department, The Canadian Press has learned. Science centre CEO Paul Kortenaar told employees at a meeting Thursday that the organization is being restructured.

item.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he's open to idea of involuntary addiction treatment
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said he’s open to the idea of involuntary addiction treatment.

item.title: Doug Ford overhauls cabinet following multiple resignations. Here is the full list
item.description: Premier Doug Ford has announced several changes to his cabinet, including moving David Piccini into a new portfolio amid an ongoing integrity commissioner investigation into his handling of the Skills Development Fund.

item.title: Progressive Conservatives, NDP hold on to their seats in Ontario byelections
item.description: Little has changed at Queen’s Park after Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s Progressive Conservatives and the Opposition New Democrats held on to their seats in three byelections Thursday.

item.title: This online ticket seller has been fined by the Ford government
item.description: Ontario has issued what could be its first fine against a ticket reselling platform under the province’s anti-scalping law, which continues to get tested as resellers look to unload tickets to upcoming events such as the Toronto International Film Festival.

item.title: Trade war with United States looms large over Ontario byelections
item.description: The escalating trade war with the United States looms large over three upcoming provincial byelections in Ontario.

item.title: Ontario spent $25K on Doug Ford’s new ‘Lake Ontario’ sign
item.description: Ontario spent $25,000 on the new 'Lake Ontario, Now and Always' sign unveiled by Premier Doug Ford over the weekend, a spokesperson from his office says.

item.title: Ford government says it will move ahead with ripping out bike lanes on stretch of Bloor Street
item.description: The Ford government says it is immediately starting to remove bike lanes along a stretch of Bloor Street West and is moving forward with plans to strip lanes from two other major Toronto arteries.

item.title: Doug Ford unveils new Lake Ontario sign and says ‘we’ll never ever back down’
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford has unveiled a new Lake Ontario sign Saturday afternoon, just days after U.S. President Donald Trump renamed the Great Lake as “Lake America.”
